title: Whether to label machine-made media
statement: Whether to label media as machine-made is unsettled: most teens say they want labels, but labels tend to lower trust in content presented as authoritative.
example: In a national survey, 73% of US teens wanted AI-generated content clearly labelled or watermarked.
detail: Research for the Grade 9 film found a nationally representative survey of US teens (January 2025) in which 73% wanted AI-generated content clearly labelled or watermarked (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0248-g9-video-research-full-files.qmd`). Experiments on disclosure point the other way: labelling content as AI-generated lowers perceived credibility and trust even when its quality is identical, and in the one field experiment with high-school students a simple label raised trust in a chatbot but lowered it for labelled news (the same file). The file's net read is that disclosure is not a free action: it can raise attention for a moment but tends to lower trust on reflection, most for content presented as authoritative, which the unit film is (the same file).
against: Most of the disclosure experiments used adults, and the one with teenagers had 60 students at one school (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0248-g9-video-research-full-files.qmd`).
